destination.name: Albury
destination.tagline: A Murray River border town with a free art museum and a big dam wall nearby.
destination.description: Albury sits on the Murray River on the New South Wales side of the Victorian border, paired with Wodonga across the water. Visitors come for Murray Art Museum Albury, which is free and open seven days, and for Hume Dam, a wall completed in 1936 that holds back Lake Hume. The town grew as a river crossing gazetted in 1839 and as the point where trains changed gauge, and the size of its station still reflects that.
whyVisit: Visit the free Murray Art Museum
Walk across the Hume Dam wall
Kayak or swim on Lake Hume

goodToKnow.title: Art museum hours
goodToKnow.detail: Murray Art Museum Albury is free and open Mon–Fri 10 am–5 pm and Sat–Sun and public holidays 10 am–4 pm.

goodToKnow.title: Hume Dam is a drive
goodToKnow.detail: The dam is about 20 minutes by car from Albury and Wodonga; the dam wall is closed to access on some days, so check before you go.

goodToKnow.title: Trains are infrequent
goodToKnow.detail: NSW TrainLink runs two services a day from Sydney and Melbourne to Albury station; the Hume Highway coach and drive from Melbourne is about 3.5 hours.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} avoid the hot, mostly dry summers and the cool, damp winters, and suit walking the dam wall and the Murray.
